questions.question: What do the  Quillfinch chicks  eat first?
questions.explanation:
Chicks eat soft larvae brought by both parents.
Seeds come later, when the beak has hardened.

questions.question: How does the Ember wren announce a nearby snake?
questions.explanation: The wren gives a rising whistle that the whole flock repeats. The drum of the wings is a courtship display.

questions.question: At what time of day does the Marsh trumpeter sing its longest song?
questions.explanation: The longest song comes at dawn, when the air over the marsh is still. Dusk songs are short.

questions.question: Why does the Tumblewing call while it rolls through the air?
questions.explanation: The calls keep a pair together over open ground. Fish do not react to the sound.

questions.question: How many notes are in the Quillfinch alarm call?
questions.explanation: The alarm call has three notes, falling in pitch. A single note is the contact call.

questions.question: Which bird sings in a lower register than the Marsh trumpeter?
questions.explanation: The Dusk heron has the deepest voice of the five. The Ember wren has the highest.

questions.question: How many eggs rest in the nest?
questions.explanation: Three pale eggs rest in the brown nest. A fourth egg is laid only in a warm year.
